topics.name: Shakespeare — one play (Macbeth, Romeo and Juliet, The Tempest, The Merchant of Venice, Much Ado About Nothing, or Julius Caesar)
The 19th-century novel — one text (e.g. A Christmas Carol, Great Expectations, Jane Eyre, Frankenstein, Pride and Prejudice, Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde, The Sign of Four)
Modern prose or drama — one text from the set list
Poetry anthology — one cluster (Love and relationships, Power and conflict, or Worlds and lives)

connections.why: Both are pre-20th-century set texts assessed for close analysis with historical context; the play builds the contextual reading the novel extends
Reading a 19th-century novel and a modern text invites comparison of how social context shapes character and theme across eras
The analytical techniques drilled on the named anthology cluster are exactly what students apply, unsupported, to unseen poems
Themes of power, love and conflict in the play recur across the poetry cluster, enabling thematic cross-reference
Modern social concerns in the set text echo the contemporary voices in the anthology
Sustained close-reading of a long novel sharpens the independent analytical instinct needed for unseen poetry
Analysing Shakespeare's imagery and form trains the language analysis transferred to unseen verse
